messages:
Matt: quick check — I'm seeing inconsistent behavior between the Python/TS SDKs and raw REST for /v1/generate around the cache flag. Anyone else run into this?

Sophia: can you paste a tiny repro? is this just the cache flag or multiple params?

Matt: minimal repro below. gist: python SDK serializes use_cache as null, TS SDK either omits or sends undefined, and curl that omits the field gets a different default. server treats null as explicit false, missing => true.

Matt: ```python
# python SDK
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-v1", input="hi", use_cache=None)
# the generated JSON body ends up with: {"use_cache": null, ...}
```

Matt: ```ts
// ts SDK
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-v1', input: 'hi' /* no useCache */ })
// JSON ends up omitting useCache (or undefined is dropped by JSON.stringify)
```

Matt: curl (raw REST):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hi"}'
# server interprets missing useCache => true (server default)
```

Lisa: that matches a change we made in Nov '25 — we intentionally treated null as an explicit opt-out. so null != missing. SDKs sending null are effectively opting out.

Reza: we should standardize SDK behavior: SDKs must omit parameters unless user explicitly sets them. i.e. don't serialize None/null for optional params. Also ensure name mapping is consistent: python use_cache -> useCache in the outgoing JSON.

Sophia: agree. quick action: python to_dict should drop keys where value is None. TS is usually fine because JSON.stringify drops undefined, but check any internal serializer that might convert undefined -> null.

Matt: i'll open a python PR to stop emitting nulls and add a unit test asserting missing keys produce server defaults. will also add an integration test hitting REST to confirm server default behavior. assigning myself.

Lisa: i'd prefer SDK fix first. changing server semantics would be risky — some clients intentionally send null to opt-out. i'll document the contract in the API guide: missing => server default, null => explicit value (false). :memo:

Reza: another gotcha: temperature and top_k — some older SDKs set defaults (0.0) which prevents server defaulting to 1.0. SDKs should use None/undefined to allow server-side defaults unless we have explicit SDK defaults we want to keep.

CI-bot: matt/py-sdk-null-fix #1234 build passed (linux, py39, unit).

Matt: thanks — i'll draft PRs for python and a quick check in TS, link this thread, and add a regression test for serialization. pinging @Sophia for review when ready.

Sophia: sounds good. ping me and i'll review. :eyes:
